step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture illustrates an end-to-end IoT monitoring and analytics pipeline on AWS. IoT devices publish MQTT temperature data to AWS IoT Core, which evaluates incoming messages using IoT Rules. The rule action streams raw data into AWS Kinesis Data Firehose (Raw). From Firehose, raw messages are stored directly into a RAW S3 bucket for long-term retention and simultaneously passed to Kinesis Data Analytics for real-time SQL analysis. Analyzed results are routed along two paths: to a second Kinesis Data Firehose (Processed) which saves JSON formatted processed events into a PROCESSED S3 bucket, and to an AWS Lambda function that writes the aggregated metrics into Amazon DynamoDB. A web application hosted via Amazon CloudFront polls DynamoDB every 10 seconds for real-time visualization, with Amazon Cognito providing user authentication.

graph.name: AWS IoT Monitoring and Visualization Pipeline
graph.notes: Real-time IoT ingestion and analytics system. Raw data from IoT Core is delivered via Kinesis Data Firehose to S3 and Kinesis Data Analytics. Analytics results feed into processed S3 storage via Firehose and to DynamoDB via Lambda. CloudFront serves a static web application that polls DynamoDB every 10 seconds, with Cognito securing user access.

edges.notes: IoT devices send MQTT messages to IoT Core.
IoT Core evaluates rules on received MQTT messages.
IoT Rule routes raw messages into Firehose.
Firehose delivers raw messages to RAW S3 bucket.
Firehose streams raw data into Kinesis Data Analytics.
Kinesis Data Analytics sends processed stream to second Firehose.
Kinesis Data Analytics invokes Lambda function with analyzed events.
Firehose persists JSON processed events to PROCESSED S3 bucket.
Lambda function writes metrics into DynamoDB table.
CloudFront web application polls DynamoDB every 10 seconds for real-time visualization data.
